title: All creatures
tomorrow: Baba Kartar's hands shake now. does he mind getting old?

cards: Somebody is talking on the back porch, and the sun isn't up. Simran pads out in her socks, phone in hand.
It's Baba Kartar, Bebe's older brother, who moved in this month when the stairs at his old place got to be too much.
He's in a plastic chair under a shawl, tearing the edge off yesterday's roti, and he's talking to the sparrows. Not muttering. Talking.

Asking the small one with the bent wing how it slept. Simran starts filming for the group chat, then stops, because he's looked up at her and asked a real question: do you think they know whose light they carry?

teach.b: She doesn't have an answer, so he gives her his, from Kirtan Sohila, the prayer before sleep. In paraphrase: among all is the light, and that light is You; by its light, everything is lit. That's Ang 13.
Everything, he says, tapping the chair. Not only people who pray. Not only people.
Then he gives her the other half, from the evening prayer, Rehras. Guru Arjan writes, in paraphrase, that God placed creatures inside rocks and stones and set their food before them. Ang 10.
The feeding was arranged before the sparrow ever reached the porch. So what's a person's part in it? Baba Kartar thinks it's small.
Notice whose light is in front of you, and don't be careless with it.

teach.h: FOOD SET OUT INSIDE THE STONE.
teach.b: Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Sikh evening prayer has a line about the food of creatures hidden inside stone.
The care reaches places nobody is watching.

teach.h: NOT A RULE FOR YOUR PLATE.
teach.b: None of this settles what goes on your plate; Sikhs differ there. It's about how you move through a world that is full of lit things.
Simran puts the phone in her pocket. The sparrow with the bent wing hops closer. Baba Kartar tears off another piece of roti and holds it out, not to the bird.

how: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila before sleep and Rehras in the evening; many Sikh households and gurdwaras put out water and grain for birds and animals as a small daily kindness.

o: only the people who pray and remember God
the animals blessed at a harvest festival
every living thing, each lit by the one light

games.q: the porch at dawn — tap the pairs.
p: food set out inside the stone
talks to the sparrows at dawn

s: in Gurbani, the divine light shines in people only
Ang 13: among all is the light; everything is lit by it.
a line in Rehras speaks of creatures in rocks and stones being fed
Guru Arjan, Ang 10: God set their food before them.
the light line is really a rule about what Sikhs may eat
Sikhs differ on diet; the line is about how you treat a lit world.

games.q: a stray cat keeps showing up at your door. your roommate says feeding it only makes it your problem. what fits today's idea best?
o: shoo it away; it isn't your responsibility.
set out water and call a local rescue to help it properly.
feed it whatever's in the fridge each night, no plan.
games.why: every creature carries the light. Baba Kartar's rule: notice it, and don't be careless with it. careful care beats careless care.

practice: If there's an animal near you, a pet, a bird at the window, a dog across the street, do one kind thing for it while the sit runs: fresh water, a slow hand, or just stillness so it isn't startled. No animal nearby?
Fill a small dish with water and set it by the door or on the sill. Keep it small and unhurried.

wordCard.voice: All creatures. In the Sikh prayers the one light shines in every creature, and its food was set out before it arrived.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: jot, light; in Kirtan Sohila, the one light that is in all.

carryVoice: Carry this: every creature carries the light, sparrows included, and the ones nobody watches. The earth week, done.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 13 (Kirtan Sohila, Raag Dhanasari, Guru Nanak: 'sabh mahi jot jot hai soi'), paraphrased
Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 10 (Rehras, Raag Gujri, Guru Arjan: creatures in rocks and stones, their food set before them), paraphrased
